newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai finmin won't pressure central bank on rates.
newsitem.headline: Thai finmin won't pressure central bank on rates.

text.p: Thai Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan said on Friday that he would not pressure the Bank of Thailand to cut current high interest rates.
Although he wanted to see rates drop to boost a slowing economy, the direction of interest rates would have to be determined by market conditions, the minister told reporters.
Many bankers and analysts have said that the central bank should cut rates to spark up the economy which they widely expected to grow below the officially forecast 6.8 percent.

Amnuay's statement followed a remark on Friday by the central bank governor Rerngchai Marakanond that he saw possibilities for a cut in rates as interbank rates in the money market were now more stable.

Thailand's lending rates averaging around 13.25 percent are among the highest in the region. The central bank maintains high rates to defend the baht against spedculative attack and to attract foreign fund inflows.
But Rerngchai made it clear he was not willing to allow the interbank rate to drop below the current level of around eight percent as the country still needed to induce foreign inflows.
Amnuay said: "I agree with the central bank that there is room for the interest rates to come down."
"But interest rates here are not controlled. Though the central bank can indirectly influence the rate, it cannot force the banks to cut rates," he added.
"And the finance ministry cannot pressure the central bank to lower rates either because monetary policy is the (Bank of Thailand's) responsibility," he said.

Bankers said they expected rates after the signal from the central bank governor to ease by 50-100 basis points this year but some said such a level of cuts would not be enough to fire up the economy much.
